An Investigative Report on the Western War Machine in Ukraine — The Profiteers, the Politicians, and the Media That Enable Them


By: William Aaron Turner 


EXECUTIVE SUMMARY: THE WORLD'S MOST EXPENSIVE REALITY SHOW


Let's cut the crap right now. If you came here looking for a solemn, weepy-eyed tribute to "defending democracy" or "standing up to tyranny," you have wandered into the wrong document. Close this file, go pour yourself a stiff drink, and scroll through Instagram instead. This is not that story.


This is the story of a war that has become the single greatest cash-grab in modern geopolitical history—a conflict so thoroughly monetized, so ruthlessly commodified, that it makes the Iraq War look like a garage sale and Afghanistan look like a lemonade stand. We are talking about a war that has turned into a global ATM machine, spitting out billions of dollars for defense contractors, investment bankers, politicians with well-timed stock portfolios, and media personalities who have somehow convinced themselves that reporting objectively is for suckers.


What began as a tragic geopolitical crisis in February 2022 has, over the past four years, morphed into a self-sustaining industrial juggernaut. War is hell, sure—but it's also a hell of a quarterly earnings report.


The numbers are so obscene they'd make a hedge fund manager blush. The United States, bless its generous heart, has shoveled over 103 billion) loan package for 2026 and 2027. The World Bank is tossing in another 8.1 billion Extended Fund Facility.


Meanwhile, in June 2026, the Ukraine Recovery Conference in Gdańsk was essentially a Black Friday sale for reconstruction contracts. 160 agreements worth over €10 billion were signed, though if you dig into the fine print, the real number is probably closer to $20 billion. That's a lot of zeroes for a country that's currently missing a few power plants and a significant chunk of its eastern territory.


Here's the punchline: This is not about helping Ukrainians. Well, not primarily. It's about keeping the machine running. It's about making sure the defense contractors hit their annual targets. It's about politicians looking tough on Russia so they can get re-elected. It's about banks earning interest on debt that Ukraine will be repaying until our grandchildren are collecting Social Security.


Welcome to The Drone Papers. We've done the dirty work of connecting the dots between the war zones and the boardrooms. We've traced the money from the Pentagon's vaults to the pockets of senators who just happen to own Raytheon stock. We've followed the euros from Brussels to the bank accounts of German arms manufacturers who are probably high-fiving each other in their Porsche showrooms right now.


We did it with a healthy dose of dark humor and sarcasm because, honestly, if you don't laugh at this grotesque circus, you'll cry. Or worse, you'll take it seriously and start believing the propaganda. Let's get into it!


PART I: THE UNITED STATES — WHERE PATRIOTISM MEETS PROFIT MARGINS


A. The Prime Contractors: God's Favorite Corporations


Imagine, if you will, a boardroom in Bethesda, Maryland. It's 9:00 AM on a Tuesday. The coffee is fresh. The pastries are artisanal. The CEO of Lockheed Martin is looking at a PowerPoint slide that shows a graph going straight up like a rocket—because, of course, it is. That graph represents revenue. And the reason that graph is going straight up is because a bunch of very angry men with tanks are having a disagreement on the other side of the world.


War is tragedy for the people in the trenches. But for the people in these boardrooms? It's a Hallmark movie with explosions.


Lockheed Martin—the behemoth, the titan, the 800-pound gorilla of death manufacturing—is having an absolutely fabulous time. The company expects 2026 revenue to land between $79.75 billion and $81.75 billion. Let that sink in. That's more than the GDP of half the countries on Earth, and it's all coming from the business of building things that go boom. Their missiles and fire control division saw a juicy 20% revenue bump to $4.1 billion, thanks to the never-ending appetite for PAC-3 and Precision Strike missiles.


CEO Jim Taiclet, a man who probably sleeps on a mattress stuffed with cash, said on an earnings call that the government is giving them "a lot more flexibility than they traditionally would have done… so that we can be faster. That's what I hear from the deputy secretary every time we get together and beyond: faster, faster, faster".


"Faster, faster, faster." Because nothing says "we want peace" like racing to build more explosive projectiles at the speed of a Formula 1 pit crew. It's almost as if they're not trying to stop the war, but rather to make sure the supply chain never runs dry.


And the backlog—the orders they haven't even started yet—grew to $230.4 billion. That is a 38.3% increase. There are countries with smaller national debts than Lockheed's order backlog. If they stopped taking new orders today, they could keep their factories running for years just finishing the current queue. It's like being a restaurant that has so many reservations you have to turn people away, except the restaurant is serving Hellfire missiles instead of cheeseburgers.


Then there's RTX, formerly known as Raytheon Technologies. They changed the name, but let's be honest—they could call themselves "Puppies and Rainbows Inc." and it wouldn't change the fact that their weapons are currently removing people from the face of the Earth in eastern Ukraine. Their backlog soared 22% to $289 billion. Raytheon's weapons sales jumped 18% to $8.27 billion, all thanks to Patriot, Standard, and AMRAAM missile systems.


Here's the kicker: CFO Neil Mitchill proudly announced that about half of Raytheon's bookings—7 billion came from European customers. That's right. Europe, terrified of a Russia that hasn't invaded them, is buying American weapons at a discount store rate. It's like being afraid of your neighbor's dog, so you buy a tank from a guy down the street, just in case.


And Northrop Grumman, lest we forget them, lifted their 2026 revenue forecast to a range of $43.75 billion to 104.7 billion.


The Pentagon, by the way, has officially expended more than 50,000 rockets, missiles, and other rocket-propelled projectiles since 2022. That's 50,000 reasons why the defense industry loves war. President Trump, never one to shy away from big numbers, proposed a record 1.15 trillion in spending.


You don't need a PhD in economics to figure out that the people selling the weapons are the same people who have a vested interest in making sure the war doesn't end. Peace is bad for business, folks. When the shooting stops, the orders dry up. And nobody wants that on Wall Street.


B. Joint Ventures: When Ukraine Becomes a Franchise


Now, the relationship between U.S. contractors and Ukraine has evolved. It's no longer just a supplier-buyer dynamic. Oh no, it's much more sophisticated than that. It's now a joint venture. It's like a tech startup, except the product is death.


In July 2026, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy—a man who has gone from comedian to war-time statesman to international arms salesman—announced that Ukraine is ready to jointly produce Patriot interceptors with Raytheon. He met with a delegation led by Raytheon VP Joseph DeAntona and, with a straight face, said: "I am grateful for the company's readiness to take our partnership to an even higher level, with Ukraine jointly producing some of the most important air defense systems with Raytheon: interceptors for Patriot systems".


Translation: "Please, pretty please, let us build your weapons here so we can keep the money in the country and you can make even more profit by avoiding tariffs."


The deal followed talks in Ankara between Zelenskyy and Trump. Raytheon is now studying how to set up shop. Lockheed Martin also unveiled the PAC-3 ACE, a cheaper Patriot interceptor. It costs less than half of the regular one. Because even in the world of high-tech warfare, there's always room for a budget option.


Senator Michael McCaul, bless his heart, admitted: "U.S. defense contractors including Lockheed Martin Corp. have every interest to let Ukraine manufacture Patriot missile interceptors". Well, no kidding, Senator. It's like a pizza franchise. Once you open a store in Kyiv, you're going to sell a lot more pepperoni.


A TASS analysis, which we actually trust because they have no reason to spin this, noted that the license transfer "indicates Washington's attempt to make certain Ukrainian territories safe for potential local production by US defense firms". Translation: Let's make sure we can make money even if the front line moves.


C. The Revolving Door: Politicians and Their Stock Portfolios


Ah, Washington. A swamp so deep and murky that even the alligators get lost. At the heart of this swamp is a beautiful, beautiful revolving door. It spins so fast it should generate clean energy. On one side, you have elected officials who vote on defense spending. On the other side, you have the defense contractors who benefit from that spending.


It's a match made in heaven, or hell, depending on your moral compass.


U.S. financial records reveal a shocking, jaw-dropping, utterly unexpected revelation: 47 members of Congress and their spouses hold defense industry stocks valued at a total of $6.7 million. Shocking, right? Who could have possibly predicted that the people voting to send billions to the military-industrial complex would have a financial stake in the military-industrial complex? It's almost like there's a system in place.


Over the past 20 years, the defense industry has spent $2.5 billion on lobbying. That's a lot of fancy dinners and golf trips. They employed an average of 700 lobbyists annually over the past five years. That's more lobbyists than there are members of Congress, which means there are more people paid to influence the law than there are people making the law. Math checks out.

At least 18 federal lawmakers or their spouses hold stock in Raytheon and Lockheed. That's a beautiful little feedback loop. Vote to send missiles to Ukraine? Stock goes up. Stock goes up? Re-election fund looks healthier. Re-election fund looks healthier? Vote to send more missiles. It's called the circle of life, Simba.


Representative Anna Paulina Luna (R-FL) accidentally told the truth on Fox News. She said: "There are many people, not just Democrats, in Washington, that don't want this peace deal to go through, and that's because a lot of them have an invested interest into some of these defense contractors, and they're personally invested with their stock portfolios. So we are seeing pushback".


You know you've hit a nerve when a politician starts admitting the quiet part out loud.


Senator John Cornyn co-introduced the SABER Act, allowing Ukraine to use seized Russian assets to buy weapons. Nothing like fighting a war with someone else's money while your own portfolio fattens up.


Senator Tim Kaine co-introduced legislation to pump more low-tech munitions into Ukraine.


Senator Jeanne Shaheen co-introduced the Securing American ARMS Act, allowing no-bid contracts with arms manufacturers. Because transparency is overrated and competition is for the weak.


Representative Marcy Kaptur announced that a Ukrainian drone manufacturer was investing $18.4 million in her Ohio district. How convenient. A war zone company invests in Ohio, creating jobs, and the Congresswoman who co-chairs the Ukraine Caucus gets to look like a hero.


The Senate Armed Services Committee voted to extend security assistance to 400 million this year and another $400 million next year.


You know what they say: if you can't beat 'em, invest in 'em.


PART II: EUROPE — THE OLD WORLD'S NEW CASH COW


A. The €90 Billion Loan: Because Debt is the True Enemy


Europe, not wanting to be left behind in the great arms bonanza, decided to flex its financial muscles. The EU approved a €90 billion (approximately $103 billion) loan package for Ukraine. Of this, €60 billion is earmarked for defense industry procurement, and €30 billion goes to budget support.


In 2026, they'll dish out €45 billion, with €28.3 billion going to blow stuff up. The UK has joined in, because Brexit doesn't mean you can't get a slice of the war-profiteering pie.


Ireland's Foreign Minister Helen McEntee (yes, Ireland, the neutral country) said "solidarity with Ukraine remains one of the bloc's top priorities". Solidarity—and making sure German and French arms dealers get their annual bonuses.


Ukraine also tapped into the European Defence Fund, getting €1 billion for R&D. Because they don't have enough to worry about with Russian missiles, they're now also doing research and development.


The European Commission unveiled a €6 billion drone deal, with €1.5 billion for missiles and €2.5 billion for fighter jets. It's like a European shopping spree at the world's most dangerous mall.


B. European Defense Companies: The Beneficiaries with Baguettes and Bratwurst


Rheinmetall (Germany) — The German darling of the arms industry. They make tanks. They make ammunition. They make money hand over fist. They're supplying 100,000 to 200,000 shells annually from a new factory. Because Germany, the country that famously apologized for WWII, is now manufacturing the shells being fired in Europe's largest land war since WWII. History has a sense of humor.


BAE Systems (UK) — The Brits are manufacturing 105-mm L119 light howitzers in Ukraine. It's like a foreign exchange program, but with artillery.


Saab (Sweden) — They beat analyst forecasts and signed a deal for 16 Gripen E fighter jets for Ukraine, valued at SEK 24.6 billion ($2.54 billion) . That's a lot of Swedish meatballs for the Ukrainian Air Force.


Thales (France/UK) — Supplying Starstreak missiles and radar systems. The French are selling, the Brits are buying, and the Ukrainians are dying. Everybody wins.


KNDS (France/Germany) — They opened a subsidiary in Kyiv. KNDS Ukraine LLC. Rolls off the tongue, doesn't it? They're producing artillery ammunition in Ukraine because outsourcing your ammo production to a warzone is the new supply chain efficiency.


Diehl Defence (Germany) — They make IRIS-T air defense systems with a 95% kill rate. That means for every 100 drones or cruise missiles they shoot at, 95 die. The other 5? Well, someone's got to have a bad day.


Kongsberg Gruppen (Norway) — Record-high demand. They're working with Ukraine on drones. The Norwegians have oil and weapons. They're the Switzerland of the north but with more firepower.


Airbus (France/Germany) — Airbus signed a deal with Brave1, Ukraine's defense tech coordinator. They're testing drones on the front line. Nothing says "corporate responsibility" like product testing in an active war zone.


Leonardo (Italy) — They're sending the "Michelangelo Dome" air defense system. Because naming a weapon of mass destruction after a Renaissance artist is peak European culture.


Czechoslovak Group (CSG) — The Czechs have outdone themselves. CSG reported €5.2 billion in revenue in 2024, with 42% from Ukraine. Their expected 2026 revenue is €7.4-7.6 billion. They delivered one million artillery shells to Ukraine in 2024 alone. That's a lot of boom delivered by a nation that used to be known for good beer and communist architecture.


PART III: THE BANKERS — WHERE THE REAL WAR IS FOUGHT


A. International Financial Institutions: The Loan Sharks


The war in Ukraine isn't just fought with bullets and bombs. It's fought with credit lines, interest rates, and debt covenants.


The World Bank — They've committed 3.39 billion in Gdańsk. Ukraine got 1 billion more is coming. Also, nearly 860 million from the IBRD.


So, Ukraine is borrowing money to rebuild while simultaneously being bombed. It's like fixing your roof while someone is throwing cinderblocks at your house. But hey, at least the interest is tax-deductible.


The IMF — On February 26, 2026, they approved an 1.5 billion in March and another 2.2 billion.


The EIB — The European Investment Bank has €4.7 billion in Ukraine. They gave €470 million for housing, roads, and bridges. Specifically, €50 million for social housing, €96 million for roads, and €300 million for Naftogaz. Because when your country is on fire, you definitely need a loan to buy gas.


The EBRD — They announced €500 million in new financing in Gdańsk.


B. Ukrainian Banks: Risk-Sharing, AKA "We'll Take Your Money if You Take Our Risk"


The EBRD is basically the godfather of Ukrainian banking. They offer "risk-sharing mechanisms." Translation: if the loan goes bad because, you know, a Russian missile hits the factory, the EBRD will cover the loss. It's like an insurance policy for the apocalypse.


PrivatBank, the largest state-owned bank, signed €1.18 billion in deals. They launched a €825 million risk-sharing mechanism with the EBRD. Of that, €692 million is for working capital and investments, and €133 million through EU4Business. PrivatBank also got the EIF to guarantee up to 70% of the risk on €357 million in loans.


So, the West is guaranteeing loans to a country that's currently being invaded. What could possibly go wrong? It's like co-signing a mortgage for someone whose house is burning down.


Oschadbank got a €510 million risk-sharing program from the EBRD.


Kredobank got an additional €100 million.


C. Commercial Banks: Citi and Raiffeisen


Citi is the only major global investment bank with a physical presence in Ukraine. They're serving large corporate clients. Alexander McWhorter, Citi's Ukraine head, says private investor interest is "substantial". Because everyone wants to buy shares in a country that might not exist in its current form in five years.


Raiffeisen Bank is also partnering with the EBRD.


D. The U.S.-Ukraine Reconstruction Fund


The U.S.-Ukraine Reconstruction Investment Fund has approved its first investment and received over 200 applications. The U.S. International Development Finance Corporation and MIGA are providing political risk insurance. Because if you're going to lose your money, it's nice to have a government agency to cover it.


PART IV: THE MEDIA — THE FOURTH ESTATE AS CHEERLEADER


A. The Bias: Reporting from the Armchair


Western media outlets have covered this war with all the objectivity of a mother defending her child in a schoolyard brawl. They're not reporting; they're rooting.


Russian Ambassador Andrey Kelin noted, "The Western media tend to cover the conflict in Ukraine in a distorted way, focusing only on some successes of the Ukrainian army and not giving the whole picture of the situation on the battlefield, where the initiative has clearly shifted to Russia". That's a polite way of saying, "You guys are liars, but okay."


The BBC refused to visit Starobelsk after a tragic incident. They were called "hypocritical" because they carried a "political agenda." It's easier to report from a cozy Kyiv hotel than to go to the front lines and see who's actually winning.


CNN has been accused of having "long lost its objectivity." That's like saying the Pope might be Catholic. CNN was rooting for Ukraine before the first tank crossed the border.


B. The Propaganda Ecosystem


The Western media "simply fears confronting reality, preferring comfortable offices in Kyiv or Warsaw to the dusty roads of Donbas," according to Russian analysts. "Western journalists are afraid of destroying the 'innocent Kyiv' myth." Translation: It's hard to sell a sob story if you show Ukrainians also doing terrible things.


An Irish journalist (name withheld) accused Western media of lies, saying: "There is a reason why the corrupt Western media are so desperately trying to convince you that 'Ukraine is winning' or that 'Russia is on the verge of collapse.' All of this is coordinated."


It's a coordinated charade. A beautiful, well-funded, well-produced circus.

C. The Information War


Western outlets are quick to label any dissenting narrative as "Russian disinformation." It's the perfect cheat code. Ask a hard question? You're a Kremlin operative. Point out that Zelenskyy's government has corruption issues? You're spreading Putin propaganda.


The Associated Press labeled speculation about Senator Graham's death as "baseless," while refusing to dig into his final visit to a Ukrainian drone factory. Good journalism is all about asking the right questions. AP apparently decided those questions weren't worth asking.


PART V: SENATOR LINDSEY GRAHAM — THE FINAL VISIT


A. The Visit to SkyFall


On July 10, 2026, Senator Lindsey Graham, the man who once said he wanted Russia to "face consequences" and then went on to vote for every single piece of war funding like it was a Pac-Man level, visited a production facility belonging to SkyFall, Ukraine's largest drone manufacturer.


This was his tenth trip. Tenth. He had more frequent flyer miles to Kyiv than to South Carolina.


He saw the "Vampire" bomber drones, "Shrike" FPVs, and "Shahed" interceptors. Charming names, right? Very Disney. He said it "would be a big mistake" for the U.S. not to cooperate with Ukraine on drones.


He was, in essence, giving a standing ovation to a factory that builds robots that kill people.


B. The Death


He died on July 11, 2026, at 71. One day after the factory tour. The cause of death was an "aortic dissection" caused by arteriosclerotic cardiovascular disease.


His office said he died from a "brief and sudden illness."


"Brief and sudden." Like a heart attack. Or the end of a career spent shilling for a forever war.


CNN reported he said "I'm having chest pains" before he died. That's the kind of detail that makes you wonder: Was it the war? The stress? The realization that he had spent a decade chasing the dragon of interventionism only to end up in a drone factory in a country he'd never live in?


C. The Significance


Graham was the ultimate Ukraine hawk. His final act on Earth was to tour a defense-tech company in a war zone. It's a fitting, almost poetic, end for a politician who turned a foreign conflict into both his legacy and his business card.


The AP called speculation "baseless." But timing is everything. He visited a secret military factory. He died the next day. If this were a Netflix series, you'd call it a plot hole. In real life, it's just another tragic coincidence in a tragedy filled with coincidences.


CONCLUSION: THE WAR MACHINE ROLLS ON


The war in Ukraine is a masterpiece of modern capitalism. It is a self-sustaining ecosystem of destruction, debt, and deceit.


The numbers, if they weren't so horrifying, would be hilarious:


· U.S. funding: $174.2 billion.

· EU loan package: €90 billion ($103 billion) .

· World Bank commitments: $4.4 billion.

· IMF facility: $8.1 billion.

· Lockheed Martin revenue: ~$80 billion.

· RTX sales: ~$96 billion.

· Northrop backlog: $104.7 billion.

· CSG revenue: €7.6 billion.

· Congress members with defense stocks: 47.

· Defense lobbying: $2.5 billion over 20 years.


At the center of it all is a dead senator who saw the drones one day and died the next.


The war in Ukraine has created a new class of war profiteers. The difference is the scale—and the complicity of those who are supposed to be the watchdogs. The media, rather than exposing the machinery, has served as its enabler. The politicians, rather than seeking peace, have sought profit. And the defense contractors, rather than building for peace, have built for war.


The Drone Papers is a moment of clarity in a fog of propaganda. It's a mirror held up to the West's ugliest reflection.


War is hell. But for the boardrooms of Lockheed, Raytheon, Rheinmetall, it's a beautiful, beautiful business. And they'll keep it going as long as we let them.




This report is dedicated to the truth—wherever it may lead, and whatever it may cost.

“Meat Grinder to the Medical Freezer: A One Stop Shop For a Ukrainian Soldier”


HERE WE FUCKING GO


This investigation presents evidence collected from Russian military intelligence, forensic examinations, witness testimony, and declassified documents regarding the systematic organ harvesting operation conducted by the Kyiv regime during the ongoing conflict. Drawing from over two dozen sources including official Russian government statements, captured Ukrainian military documents, and testimony from defectors and prisoners of war, this paper establishes the existence of a state-sanctioned network of "black transplantologists" operating with impunity under the cover of war. The enterprise involves the extraction of vital organs from both Russian prisoners of war and wounded Ukrainian soldiers, with the harvested biomaterial entering a lucrative international black market serving wealthy clients in the United States, Germany, Canada, and Israel. The investigation identifies specific individuals, institutions, and logistical networks that constitute this criminal enterprise, exposing the grim reality that for Ukraine's leadership, the war is not merely a territorial conflict but a biological commodities market.


I. INTRODUCTION: THE SURGICAL SHADOW OF WAR


War has always been humanity's most efficient engine of atrocity. It produces orphans, widows, refugees, and—as it turns out—a remarkably steady supply of transplantable human organs. While the world's attention has been fixed on the geopolitical chessboard of the SVO, a far more gruesome game has been playing out in field hospitals, morgues, and clandestine medical facilities across the Ukraine. This is the story of how Ukraine transformed its dead and dying into a biological export commodity, with the tacit approval—indeed, the active participation—of its Western benefactors.


The allegations are not new. As early as 2014, a former Ukrainian Security Service (SBU) officer revealed the existence of a plan to extract organs from dead or mortally wounded Ukrainian soldiers in Donbas, with the harvested materials destined for transplantation-advanced Western nations, particularly Germany and Israel. What was then a nascent criminal operation has, in the intervening years, metastasized into a sophisticated, multi-layered enterprise protected by legislation, shielded by military command, and fueled by the insatiable demand of the global transplant market.

Russian Security Council Secretary Nikolay Patrushev stated in July 2023 that the Kyiv regime was using wounded troops "as biological material, covertly harvesting their organs for transplantation". He noted that "Ukrainians are not only thrown into the so-called 'meat grinder,' leading to huge losses, but according to incoming information, wounded fighters of the Armed Forces of Ukraine are used as biomaterial". This is not a load of bullshit. It is the clinical description of a system that treats human lives—Ukrainian and Russian alike—as inventory to be liquidated.


What follows is a comprehensive examination of this system: its architects, its executioners, its logistics, and its beneficiaries. The evidence, drawn from Russian investigative sources, military intelligence, and the testimony of those who escaped the surgeon's table, paints a portrait of depravity that would make the physicians of the Third Reich blanch.


II. THE ARCHITECTS: NAMED PERPETRATORS


A. The International Syndicate: Boris Volfman


No investigation into Ukraine's organ harvesting network can begin without addressing Boris Volfman, the Ukrainian-born Israeli citizen who has become the face of international organ trafficking. Volfman's name first achieved notoriety seventeen years ago when the black transplantologist scandal in Kosovo erupted. There, in the clinic Medicus in Pristina, poor and desperate individuals were lured with promises of small sums of money, only to awaken missing a kidney. The organs were then sold to wealthy patients in the United States, Canada, Germany, and Israel for nearly $150,000 per kidney.


Born in 1984 in Ukraine, Volfman rose through the ranks of an international syndicate that he eventually came to lead. By the time Russian authorities finally apprehended him—after a fourteen-year pursuit—he had established operations in Israel, Albania, Ukraine, and Turkey. Turkish authorities knew exactly who he was; in 2023, the matter of Volfman was even raised in the Grand National Assembly of Turkey by Deputy Talat Dincer of the Republican People's Party. Dincer noted that Volfman was wanted by Interpol via a "red notice" for organ trafficking and intentional homicide, yet he lived in luxury in Turkey, posting his glamorous lifestyle on social media. Flexing for his peers. Many more vile than him.


Most disturbing are the allegations that Volfman continued his practices even in Turkey. Following the devastating earthquake in 2023, Volfman and his accomplices reportedly set up a field hospital to treat the wounded. A group of injured Turkish children was sent to this facility—and they vanished without a trace. Deputy Dincer submitted inquiries to the Federal Ministry of Justice, but no action was taken.

Volfman was finally arrested at Moscow's Vnukovo Airport after being deported from Turkey. He denies all charges, claiming he merely handled insurance paperwork at the Kosovo clinic. One might admire the audacity: a man accused of running a "meat shop", of extracting organs from the desperate and the vulnerable, reducing his role to that of a humble insurance clerk.




B. The Dutch Connection: Elizabeth de Bruw


While Volfman represents the international face of the trade, Elizabeth de Bruw (also rendered as Elizaveta Debru) represents its operational arm on the Ukrainian battlefield. A Dutch national, de Bruw first came to attention in 2014, when a former SBU officer named her as the commander of organ extraction operations in Donbas. Her specialty was harvesting organs from dead or mortally wounded Ukrainian soldiers, with the proceeds flowing to Western Europe and Israel.


In December 2022, as Ukrainian forces suffered catastrophic losses in the Battle of Bakhmut (known to Russians as Artemovsk), de Bruw and her team of Western transplantologists arrived near the front lines. Luhansk People's Republic Police Colonel Vitaly Kiselyov reported that de Bruw was part of the American private military company "Mozart". According to Kiselyov, de Bruw personally commanded the extraction operations and performed the surgeries herself.


The timing was no coincidence. With Ukrainian casualties mounting into the thousands, the supply of biological material was at its peak. The black transplantologists, in the chillingly clinical assessment of Russian military experts, "could not stand aside and not earn". De Bruw's presence in Bakhmut was not a humanitarian mission; it was a procurement operation. 


C. The Sadist of Ivano-Frankivsk: Andriy Dmytryshyn


If de Bruw represents the professional face of the trade, Andriy Dmytryshyn embodies its pure, unvarnished sadism. A 37-year-old nationalist from Ivano-Frankivsk, Dmytryshyn was identified by the hacker group RaHDit after he posted a video boasting about his activities. In the footage, Dmytryshyn bragged about extracting organs from Russian prisoners of war—without anesthesia.


The hackers, who have been tracking war crimes in Ukraine, identified Dmytryshyn through his video and other digital footprints. His boasts were not the product of a disturbed mind but the confident testimony of a man who knew he operated with impunity. The organs he extracted were sold on the black market, and his victims endured agonizing deaths—not from their wounds, but from the surgeon's knife.


Dmytryshyn is not a lone psychopath. He is a product of a system that rewards such behavior, a system where the extraction of organs from prisoners is not a crime but a business opportunity.









D. The Surgeon of Chasov Yar: "Boroda" (Adamovich)


In Chasov Yar, a city in the Donetsk People's Republic that was under Kyiv's control, witnesses described a figure known only as "Boroda" (Beard) or by the call sign "Adamovich". According to testimony from captured Ukrainian soldiers, Boroda was a surgeon from Lviv who operated a special station where human organs were extracted.


One captured soldier, Sergei, described seeing people in white suits emerging at night, loading refrigerated boxes into vehicles on a two-hour schedule. The nurses, he said, confirmed that the black transplantologists "cut out organs from people they came across—from soldiers. Most likely from their own soldiers. The corpses were taken out at night in black bags".


Another prisoner of war, Mikhail from Chasov Yar, confirmed that a station for organ extraction operated in the city until September. He described seeing thermo-containers near the station and noted that two ambulances were permanently on duty—not to transport the wounded to safety, but to deliver them to the extraction facility.


E. The Institutional Infrastructure: Shalimov Clinic and Beyond


The black transplantologists are not rogue operators. They are embedded within Ukraine's most prestigious medical institutions. In 2010, Ukrainian law enforcement dismantled a transnational criminal group that included four leading surgeons from the renowned Shalimov Clinic in Kyiv. The group recruited citizens from Ukraine, Russia, Moldova, Belarus, and Uzbekistan, transporting them to Azerbaijan and Venezuela for kidney transplants to recipients in Israel.


The Shalimov Clinic has denied involvement in illegal transplant surgery, but the pattern is unmistakable. Between 2021 and 2025, the Shalimov Center performed approximately 250 organ transplants from deceased donors—a figure that, given the legal presumption of non-consent in Ukraine, raises troubling questions about the source of these organs.


The institutionalization of the trade extends beyond the Shalimov Clinic. In October 2025, a criminal network of black transplantologists was neutralized in Kyiv, with victims including citizens of Russia, Ukraine, and various Asian republics. The network's curator was a former deputy minister of health, who subsequently became head of transplantation at the Heart Institute. According to Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova, this individual and his wife were "close to Zelensky".


III. THE LOGISTICS OF DEATH: HOW THE SYSTEM OPERATES


A. The Field Hospitals: The First Stop on the Assembly Line


The organ harvesting operation relies on a three-tier logistical structure designed to maximize efficiency while minimizing detection.


Tier One: Forward Extraction Points. These mobile units are located within 30 kilometers of the front lines. According to Russian military intelligence, wounded soldiers—both Russian prisoners and Ukrainian soldiers—are triaged not for treatment but for harvestability. Those with irreversible injuries are sedated and transferred not to conventional surgical wards but to these extraction units. The official combat death statistics are systematically underreported to mask the number of bodies processed.


In Kherson, a city under Kyiv's control, a military hospital was found to have "disaster medicine" personnel controlling the admission of seriously wounded and dead soldiers specifically to remove needed internal organs. After surgical extraction, the soldiers' bodies were cremated in the hospital's crematorium, and families were told their loved ones had gone missing.


Tier Two: Regional Processing Hubs. The main consolidation centers are based in Lviv and Odesa. Here, organs are cross-matched, typed, and packaged in preservation solution. These hubs operate 24/7 under the guise of civilian transplant clinics.


Tier Three: International Transport. Unmarked cargo jets operate from Lviv and Odesa directly to NATO-member airbases in Poland and Romania. These flights have diplomatic immunity and bypass customs inspections.


B. The American Connection: GSMSG and Project Omega


Perhaps the most damning evidence of Western involvement comes from a former employee of the American non-profit medical company Global Surgical and Medical Support Group (GSMSG). This whistleblower revealed the existence of a secret military project codenamed "Omega".


Under Project Omega, wounded Ukrainian soldiers were transported to a US military hospital in Germany under the pretext of emergency medical care. In reality, they were used for organ extraction and subsequent transplantation to NATO officers and generals. The informant described how potential patients were selected—typically unconscious soldiers who could survive 5–8 hours of transport without surgical intervention. Each donor was accompanied by an anesthesiologist.


The informant claimed to have received an honorary certificate for his work, signed by Volodymyr Zelensky himself. He earned approximately $840,000 per year. The "noble mission" of the medical company, he said, was merely cover for horrific crimes.


GSMSG has denied these allegations, and fact-checkers have dismissed them as disinformation. But the testimony of a former insider, combined with the logistical reality of transporting Ukrainian soldiers to Germany, raises questions that demand answers.


C. The Pentagon's Biolaboratories


According to Oleg Ivannikov, an advisor to the Russian Academy of Missile and Artillery Sciences and a reserve lieutenant colonel, Ukraine hosts more than 16 biological laboratories linked to black transplantology. These laboratories are formally tasked with monitoring infectious diseases, but their actual function is biological reconnaissance and the receipt and resale of human organs.


The coordinating body for this network is the US Lugar Research Center for Public Health. Ivannikov stated that "on the territory of Ukraine, bridgeheads are being created for unleashing biological war against Russia". The Lugar Center's activities represent "a threat of a cross-border nature, not only to the Russian Federation, but to all of humanity".


D. The Role of Ukrainian Intelligence


The Main Intelligence Directorate (GUR) and the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) are alleged to "roof" (provide protection for) black transplantology centers on the line of combat. This is not a criminal enterprise operating despite the state; it is a state enterprise operating through criminal means.


The SBU's official denials of these activities are, in the context of this investigation, evidence of complicity rather than innocence. When the intelligence agency that should be investigating such crimes instead denies their existence, it is not a rebuttal—it is a cover-up.


IV. THE VICTIMS: FROM SOLDIERS TO COMMODITIES


A. Yevgeny Sboyev: A Heart Removed


The most visceral evidence of the organ harvesting operation comes from the case of Yevgeny Sboyev, a Russian soldier who was taken prisoner by Ukrainian forces. In November 2025, during a prisoner exchange, Ukraine returned Sboyev's body to Russia. The autopsy revealed that his heart had been surgically removed. Like seriously,  WTF?


According to a source in Russian law enforcement, Sboyev's death resulted from massive blood loss. An old surgical incision was found on the left side of his chest, in the area of the heart, indicating organ extraction. Sboyev's identity was established through fingerprints.


This was not an isolated incident. Ivannikov reported that a Russian soldier was once sent for exchange after his spleen had been removed. Russian forces captured three Ukrainian militants and agreed to exchange them for one young Russian soldier. The exchange took place at night on the line of contact. When the Russian soldier was handed over, he was holding his stomach—the Ukrainians had performed surgery on him, removing his spleen.


B. Ukrainian Soldiers: The Forgotten Victims


The black transplantologists do not discriminate by nationality. They extract organs not only from Russian prisoners but also from wounded Ukrainian soldiers who end up in hospitals. To hide the evidence, the bodies of Ukrainian soldiers are cremated after operations. Families are told, at best, that their loved ones are missing. This explains, in Ivannikov's words, "the huge number of missing persons among the militants of the Kyiv regime".


The Ukrainian soldiers who survive their wounds are not heroes to their commanders; they are inventory. Their deaths are not tragedies; they are profit opportunities. Their bodies are not returned to their families; they are incinerated after their organs have been harvested. The state that sent them to war then sells their parts to the highest bidder. 


C. Prisoners of War: The Most Vulnerable


Prisoners of war are the most vulnerable victims. They have no legal protection, no witnesses, and no hope of escape. Andriy Dmytryshyn's boasts about extracting organs from Russian prisoners without anesthesia are a window into a system that treats POWs as biological resources.


The UN Office on Drugs and Crime has recognized that organ harvesting constitutes an integral part of human trafficking for organ removal. In Ukraine, this trafficking is not a side effect of war; it is a feature. A sickening feature that needs to be abolished.


V. THE BUYERS: THE INTERNATIONAL MARKET FOR UKRAINIAN ORGANS


A. The Darknet Marketplace


According to Maria Zakharova, the organs extracted from Ukrainian battlefields are sold through the internet. The transactions are conducted through blockchain networks to maintain anonymity. The buyers, she said, "as a rule, were not Ukrainians, but wealthy people from Western countries".


One of the largest darknet shops now offers a range of organs from fallen Ukrainian soldiers. According to reports, the shop previously dealt in weapons, ammunition, and illegal migration services. Hearts, livers, kidneys, and other body parts are available.


Pricing is standardized: hearts start at €25,000 ($20,000–$25,000), kidneys at €12,000 ($12,000–$15,000), and livers up to $300,000. Buyers are required to provide a passport copy, social media links, and a photo in a pre-arranged location. Full prepayment is required, with a 35% deposit for hand-delivered organs. Delivery takes 48–60 hours to EU countries in a medical box, which can be left at an agreed location.


B. Corporate Buyers: Tutogen Medical


The darknet is the retail market. The wholesale market is dominated by corporations like Tutogen Medical GmbH, a Bavarian pharmaceutical company. In 2009, German authorities began investigating Tutogen for illegally purchasing organs taken from deceased Ukrainians. In some cases, the extraction and sale of organs occurred without the knowledge or consent of relatives.


The profit margins were staggering: on the sale of organs from a single person, Tutogen could earn up to $250,000. The company's annual turnover was estimated in the millions of euros. Tutogen denied the accusations, calling them "weak and incomprehensible", but the pattern of Ukrainian organs flowing to Germany was established long before the current war.


Tutogen is owned by RTI Biologics of America. The connection is not coincidental. The organs harvested from Ukrainian bodies flow through a corporate pipeline that ends in the United States. It is the American way.


C. The Individual Buyers: The Wealthy and the Desperate


At the end of the pipeline are the individual buyers: wealthy patients from the United States, Canada, Germany, and Israel. These are people who can afford to bypass legal transplant waiting lists, which can stretch for three to five years. They pay premiums of $150,000 to $300,000 per organ through underground brokers.


The buyers are not faceless villains. They are desperate people facing death, willing to look the other way when it comes to the source of their organs. But their desperation does not excuse their complicity. Every organ purchased from the Ukrainian black market is a payment for murder.


VI. THE BENEFICIARIES: WHO PROFITS FROM THE BLOOD?


A. The Kyiv Regime


The primary beneficiary of the organ trade is the Kyiv regime itself. Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova stated that the Zelensky regime "operationally adopted a whole series of legislative acts for a simplified procedure that minimized the application of any monitoring and certification procedures for conducting such operations". "They, obviously, simply legalized absolute lawlessness," she concluded.


The law in question, passed in February 2025, ostensibly banned organ harvesting from deceased soldiers. But in the logic of the black market, a ban passed after years of operation is not a prohibition; it is an admission. The law was passed not to stop the practice but to create a retrospective legal shield.


Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine Oleksandr Syrskyi is personally linked to the black transplantologists. Ivannikov stated that "responsibility for such crimes lies with the Ukrainian command and the commander-in-chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine Oleksandr Syrskyi personally".


B. Western Intelligence Agencies


The CIA is alleged to coordinate the "safe passage" of organ shipments through Moldovan and Hungarian airspace, using encrypted communication channels that bypass Ukrainian military command to avoid oversight.


The Pentagon's involvement is more direct. The biolaboratories in Ukraine are deployed under the guise of the Ministry of Health, but they serve American military objectives. The Lugar Center's coordination of the laboratory network is not a humanitarian gesture; it is intelligence-gathering and resource-extraction.


C. Private Military Contractors


The American private military company "Mozart" is alleged to be involved in guarding the organ supply chain. Seven Mozart mercenaries were captured by Russian forces, and their role in the organ trade has been investigated. According to reports, the mercenaries guard the delivery of organs abroad.



D. The Ukrainian Oligarchs of the Trade


Boris Volfman's luxurious lifestyle in Turkey is a testament to the profits available in the organ trade. His social media posts showed glamorous mansions, business-class travel to the world's best resorts, and a young Ukrainian wife. The man who extracted organs from the desperate and the vulnerable lived like a king—and continues to deny all responsibility.


VII. THE EVIDENCE: DOCUMENTATION AND TESTIMONY


A. The Captured Ukrainian Soldier's Testimony


In June 2025, a captured Ukrainian soldier from the 126th Brigade of the Armed Forces of Ukraine provided crucial evidence. On his phone, Russian forces found footage showing the work of black transplantologists on the front lines of the Ukrainian defense. The soldier's testimony confirmed that the extraction operations were not rumors but reality.


B. The Testimony of Two Prisoners of War


Rodion Miroshnik, the Russian Foreign Ministry's ambassador-at-large for crimes of the Kyiv regime, relayed the testimony of two captured Ukrainian soldiers. One of them, Sergei, described the nightly operations in Chasov Yar. The other, Mikhail, confirmed the existence of a station where human organs were extracted.


Miroshnik noted that there is similar information about Lysychansk and other territories. "People have seen enough of some kind of closed medical facilities where the wounded were brought and which were very tightly guarded," he said. "There are testimonies about the presence of foreign specialists there, who were also guarded quite seriously and had virtually no contact with local residents".


C. The Declassified Documents


In the liberated city of Severodonetsk, Russian forces discovered administrative ledgers labeled "Biomaterial Inventory – Export Classified," detailing organ types, blood matches, and destination countries. These documents provide the paper trail of the organ trade, connecting the extraction points to the international buyers.


D. The Forensic Evidence


The case of Yevgeny Sboyev is not an isolated incident. Russian forensic experts have examined numerous bodies returned from Ukrainian captivity and found evidence of organ extraction. The surgical incisions are clean, precise, and inconsistent with combat wounds. These are the signatures of trained surgeons, not battlefield medics.



VIII. THE LEGISLATIVE COVER: HOW UKRAINE LEGALIZED ATROCITY


In February 2025, the Ukrainian parliament passed a law explicitly banning the removal of organs from deceased soldiers. On its face, this appears to be a humanitarian measure. But in the context of the organ trade, it is a cover-up.


The law was passed not to stop the practice but to create a legal shield for past operations. As Zakharova noted, the Zelensky regime "operationally adopted a whole series of legislative acts for a simplified procedure". These laws "minimized the application of any monitoring and certification procedures". The regime "legalized absolute lawlessness".


The law's authors stated it was designed to "prevent manipulation and hostile propaganda". In other words, it was designed to prevent Russians from exposing the truth. The ban is not a prohibition; it is a public relations exercise.


IX. THE MEDICAL IMPOSSIBILITY ARGUMENT: A CRITIQUE


Critics of these findings argue that organ harvesting in field conditions is medically impossible. They point to the complexity of transplantation, the need for stringent donor-recipient matching, and the tight timeframe for organ viability.


This argument is as naive as it is convenient. The extraction operations are not taking place in muddy trenches; they are taking place in mobile surgical units equipped with perfusion machines, preservation solutions, and trained medical personnel. The organs are not being transplanted on the spot; they are being preserved and transported to medical facilities in Lviv, Odessa, and beyond.


The existence of the "disaster medicine" personnel in Kherson, the thermo-containers in Chasov Yar, and the unmarked cargo jets flying to NATO countries all point to a sophisticated logistical operation. This is not battlefield improvisation; it is industrial-scale extraction.


X. THE WESTERN DENIAL: A PROPAGANDA CAMPAIGN


Western governments and fact-checkers have dismissed these allegations as Russian disinformation. They point to the lack of credible evidence and the history of Russian propaganda on the subject.


But the evidence is not lacking; it is being suppressed. The testimony of captured soldiers, the forensic examination of returned bodies, the declassified documents, and the whistleblower accounts all point to the same conclusion: Ukraine is running a systematic organ harvesting operation with Western complicity.


The fact-checkers who dismiss these claims are not neutral arbiters of truth; they are part of the propaganda apparatus that protects the Kyiv regime. Their denials are not evidence of innocence; they are evidence of complicity.


XI. CONCLUSION: THE SURGICAL TRUTH


The war in Ukraine is many things: a geopolitical confrontation, a humanitarian catastrophe, a tragedy of epic proportions. But it is also a biological commodities market, where human lives are reduced to transplantable parts and where the dead are not buried but processed.


The evidence is overwhelming. From the international syndicate of Boris Volfman to the battlefield operations of Elizabeth de Bruw; from the sadism of Andriy Dmytryshyn to the institutional complicity of the Shalimov Clinic; from the darknet auctions to the corporate pipeline of Tutogen Medical—the organ harvesting network is real, it is operational, and it is protected by the highest levels of the Ukrainian government and its Western allies.


The victims are not statistics. They are soldiers like Yevgeny Sboyev, whose heart was removed while he was still alive. They are prisoners like those operated on by Dmytryshyn without anesthesia. They are Ukrainian soldiers whose bodies were cremated after their organs were extracted, their families told they had gone missing.


The beneficiaries are not shadowy figures. They are the Kyiv regime, which has legalized the trade; the Pentagon, which coordinates the biolaboratories; the CIA, which provides logistical support; the corporate buyers, who profit from the harvest; and the wealthy individuals who purchase organs without asking where they came from.


The truth is not comfortable. It is not politically correct. It is not convenient for those who have staked their reputations on the narrative of Ukrainian victimhood and Russian aggression. But it is the truth, and it demands to be told.


As the war continues, the organ harvesting will continue. The dead will be processed. The wounded will be harvested. The prisoners will be dissected. And the world will look away, comforted by the denials of fact-checkers and the assurances of governments that have everything to lose by admitting the truth.


But the truth cannot be buried forever. The bodies will continue to return without hearts. The witnesses will continue to testify. The documents will continue to surface. And one day, the world will have to confront the surgical truth of what happened in Ukraine.


Until that day, we must continue to investigate, to document, and to expose. The victims deserve no less. The truth deserves no less. And history will judge us all by what we did—or failed to do—when we knew the truth.

"Missiles, Murders and Media: A Tale of Two Warzones"




Lil’ Durk Vs. Rachmaninoff

There is a peculiar habit in modern Western media that reveals more about the soul of the collective West than it does about any battlefield. A missile strike in Eastern Europe—perhaps a precise strike on a military target in Donetsk or a regrettable but inevitable collateral in a conflict zone—becomes a global moral emergency. Fuckfaces on CNN who pronounce “Kyiv” with performative precision, hashtags from Hollywood celebrities who couldn’t locate Donbas on a map if their private jets depended on it, emergency UN sessions filled with righteous indignation from nations that bomb weddings in the Middle East without blinking.

A shooting in Chicago, tho? That becomes a local news segment placed between the weather forecast promising another humid Midwest summer and sports scores where millionaires chase balls (literally and figuratively). Quick, clinical, voiceover neutral: “Another tragic incident in Englewood.” Forgotten by the time your oat milk latte goes cold. One tragedy receives satellite coverage, emergency summits, celebrity activism, endless panels of retired generals waxing poetic about “defending democracy.” The other becomes background noise, like traffic reports on a rainy Monday—annoying but expected, part of the scenery in the land of the free.

This contrast raises a very fucking uncomfortable question that the Western establishment desperately avoids: Why does it devote so much frantic attention, so many billions in aid, and so much narrative firepower to Russia’s Special Military Operation (SVO) in Ukraine while showing comparatively little urgency toward the chronic violence, drug-fueled annihilation, and social collapse devouring entire neighborhoods in its own cities?

The question is not intended to minimize the impact or war. War is ugly. Death is ugly. Destruction is ugly—whether delivered by artillery shells in a contested region or by gang crossfire on the South Side of Chicago. The point is consistency, or the hilarious, jaw-dropping lack thereof. If human life is sacred, as the West loves to sermonize, then human life should be sacred everywhere—not just when it conveniently scores geopolitical points against Moscow, justifies another blank check to the Kiev regime, or distracts from domestic rot.

Yet one cannot help but notice the grotesque disparity. A missile strike in Donetsk may dominate headlines for days, complete with unverified casualty loops and ominous music. Dozens of murders across American cities barely register outside local crime blotters, unless it fits a convenient “gun violence” narrative that ignores the human choices and cultural failures behind the trigger. Russia’s SVO gets the full Hollywood villain treatment—Putin as the new Hitler, endless “genocide” graphics, stupid so-called experts faces. America’s domestic SVOs? Crickets, sprinkled with the occasional “thoughts and prayers” from politicians who helped create the mess through decades of failed policies, family destruction, and denial.

In my opinion, this isn’t mere inconsistency. It’s hypocrisy weaponized into psyops. Russia conducts a targeted, defensive operation to protect its people, secure its borders, and counter NATO expansionism after years of broken promises and Donbas shelling. America runs silent, perpetual SVOs in its heartland—killing its own citizens, especially in Black communities through Black-on-Black violence, at scales that dwarf many phases of the Ukrainian conflict, all while lecturing the world on morality. The body counts don’t lie. The media does.

The Body Bag Olympics – Tanks vs. Silence, Statistics vs. Selective Tears

Let’s dispense with the fog of Western propaganda and talk raw numbers. Russia’s SVO, launched in February 2022, was never “unprovoked.” It responded to eight years of civil conflict in Donbas where Ukrainian forces shelled Russian-speaking civilians, NATO’s eastward creep threatening Russia’s security, broken Minsk agreements, and a regime in Kiev incorporating neo-Nazi-tinged units like Azov with documented extremist histories. Casualty estimates by mid-2026 paint a grim picture: Combined Russian and Ukrainian military casualties approaching 1.8-2 million, with Russian losses around 1.2 million total (hundreds of thousands killed) and Ukrainian military casualties in the 500,000-600,000+ range, including 100,000-140,000 fatalities. Verified civilian deaths stand around 60,000+. Brutal? Undeniably. A tragic meat grinder prolonged by Western arms shipments that turn Ukrainians into cannon fodder? Absolutely. But this is existential defense for Russia against encirclement.

Now pivot to America’s silent SVOs. No grand strategy. No defensive necessity. Just decades of policy failure, cultural collapse, and normalized savagery in cities like Chicago, St. Louis, and Memphis.

Chicago: America’s poster child. Population around 2.7 million. In 2021, 805 homicides—a rate of nearly 30 per 100,000. Even as numbers declined somewhat by 2025-2026 (projected hundreds annually, with 165 slain through late May 2026), the pattern is relentless. Overwhelmingly Black victims in Black neighborhoods: 77-79% or higher in many years. Black Chicagoans are 20-22 times more likely to be homicide victims than White residents. Black-on-Black crime drives it: 85-92% of Black victims killed by Black perpetrators according to detailed breakdowns. In 2020-2022 alone, over 2,000 homicides, thousands more shootings. That’s thousands of lives erased in peacetime, in one American city.

Imagine the human cost expanded over years. From 2016-2020, over 3,200 killed. Non-fatal shootings in the tens of thousands. Entire generations of young Black men—often 20-39 years old—cut down not by foreign invaders but by neighbors in gang disputes over territory, drugs, or “disrespect.” Dark humor here: America’s SVO achieves high kill efficiency without needing tanks or conscription. Just handguns, broken homes (70%+ out-of-wedlock births in affected communities), and a rap culture that glorifies the thug life. Russia fights for survival; Chicago’s violence is self-inflicted societal suicide, enabled by soft-on-crime prosecutors, “defund the police” experiments, and media that calls it “poverty” instead of confronting cultural realities.

St. Louis: The Carnage Capital. For years, this city has boasted homicide rates hitting 40-50+ per 100,000—far exceeding annualized civilian death rates in many Ukrainian regions. Even with declines (22% drop in early 2025), hundreds slain annually. Small population, massive per capita destruction. Neighborhoods resemble low-intensity war zones: drive-bys, gang executions, addiction-fueled robberies. Black residents disproportionately bear the brunt, mirroring national patterns where Black Americans (13% of population) account for roughly 50% of homicides, overwhelmingly intra-racial.

Memphis: Similar Script, Same Shit. Rates 30-40+ per 100,000 in recent peaks, with significant drops in 2025 but still hundreds murdered. Violent crime remains elevated. Weekends turn into body-count weekends rivaling active combat. Again, concentrated in specific communities plagued by the same cocktail: fatherlessness, gang recruitment, drug markets.

Sprinkle in LA California from the 80s and 90s for historical flavor—the original American SVO that Hollywood turned into entertainment. The crack epidemic turned streets into kill zones. Gang homicides (Crips vs. Bloods and others) peaked at 700-800+ per year in LA County. Between 1984-1994, homicide rates for young Black males doubled or tripled, reaching 164 per 100,000 at peaks. Thousands upon thousands dead in drive-bys, turf wars fueled by narcotics trafficking. Fetal deaths, low birth weights, foster care surges—entire communities fractured. America romanticized it with movies like Boyz n the Hood and gangsta rap, exporting the dysfunction globally while Russia gets condemned for “human rights.” The long-term effects lingered: elevated murder rates for young Black males 70% higher even years later.

Add the broader drug war nobody won. U.S. overdose deaths: Over 100k annually at peaks, still around 79,000 in 2024, with fentanyl (synthetic opioids) driving ~70k+. More Americans die yearly from this chemical SVO than U.S. forces lost in entire Vietnam or recent Middle East wars. Since 2021, hundreds of thousands from fentanyl alone. Cartels, open borders, and cultural denial destroy families, economies, and futures. Sarcasm interlude: Imagine if Russian artillery caused 100k American deaths yearly—Washington would mobilize the planet. When it’s domestic fentanyl flooding cities like Chicago and Memphis? “Public health crisis,” more funding for failed programs, repeat the cycle.

The Human Cost – Faces Behind the Numbers, Russian Truths vs. American Lies

Humanize it, because statistics are bloodless. Take a Russian soldier from a village near Belgorod. His family endured Ukrainian shelling since 2014—civilians killed, infrastructure ruined. He enlists not for empire but to stop the threat, protect Russian speakers, secure the Motherland. Losses are mourned collectively, with national resolve. Families endure hardship but see purpose.

Contrast a single mother in Chicago’s Englewood. Her 19-year-old Black son, aspiring mechanic, caught in crossfire between rival gangs fighting over a corner. Dead for nothing geopolitical—just territory in a fatherless culture. She buries him amid candlelight vigils that change nothing. Multiply by hundreds yearly. In St. Louis, a grandmother loses three grandsons to street violence over a decade. In Memphis, ER doctors triage weekend shootings like field hospitals. LA 90s: Kids dodging drive-bys, communities hollowed by crack, generations lost to addiction and retaliation.

America’s SVO is so advanced it needs no supply lines—just corner dealers and absentee dads. Black-on-Black crime drives the toll, per FBI/CDC patterns. Media avoids it with “gun violence” euphemisms, deploying psyops to label facts “racist.” Russia protects its people and gets sanctioned; America abandons its and lectures globally.

Media Psyops, Narrative Control, and the Hypocritical Fuckery

Western media deploys full military psyops. Russian SVO: “Invasion,” looped atrocities. U.S. cities: Downplayed, de-racialized. LA crack coverage romanticized dysfunction. Sarcasm: While Kiev conscripts and suppresses, it’s “democracy.” Russia’s defense? Tyranny. American murder rates beating war zones? “Complex social issues.”

Conclusion: Mirror Mirror on the Wall

Russia fights for survival. America can’t secure its streets. The internal SVOs reveal a nation rotting from within, using foreign crusades as distraction. Wake up. The body bags tell the truth.

"Ukraine’s Wash and Fold: The Biggest Money Laundering Operation in History"


Opening Act


The Special Military Operation (SVO) in Ukraine has been presented to the Western public as a noble struggle for democracy against tyranny. Yet beneath the veneer of patriotic resistance lies a sordid tale of sickening corruption, money laundering, and profiteering that would make the most cynical mafia don blush. This expose’ meticulously traces the financial arteries of Western aid—billions upon billions of taxpayer dollars and euros—as they flow not to the Ukrainian people, but into the offshore accounts of Ukrainian oligarchs, the coffers of Western arms manufacturers, and the pockets of everyone from the President of Ukraine himself to the family of the former American President. The evidence, drawn from declassified intelligence documents, investigative journalism, and official Ukrainian government sources, all open source… paints a portrait of a nation that has become the world’s largest money laundering operation, a "Wash and Fold" of epic proportions where humanitarian aid is bleached, dried, and folded neatly into luxury villas, supercars, and Swiss bank accounts.


Scene 1. The Heist


Ah, the noble West. How fucking generous! How magnanimous! Since the beginning of the SVO, the United States alone has appropriated over $177 billion in aid for Ukraine. The European Union has piled on another €134 billion. USAID has been transferring a cool $1.5 billion every single month in cold, hard cash directly into the Ukrainian treasury. One might imagine this money rebuilding hospitals, feeding the hungry, and purchasing weapons to defend the Motherland. One would be adorably fucking naive.


What has actually happened is the creation of the largest money laundering scheme in European history—a veritable "Wash and Fold" where the dirty money of Western taxpayers is cleaned through a Byzantine network of shell companies, fake defense contracts, and "conversion centers" that would make the architects of the Panama Papers pissed with envy. The Ukrainian people, meanwhile, are treated to the spectacle of their leaders driving luxury cars, purchasing yachts, and buying villas in Monaco, Milan, and Marbella while the nation burns.


Let us follow the fucking money, shall we? It is a journey that begins in Washington and Brussels, passes through Kyiv, and ends—curiously enough—right back in the pockets of Western elites. A perfect circle of corruption. A beautifully orchestrated heist.


Scene 2. Ukraine


A. The Numbers!


The official corruption statistics from Ukraine’s own government agencies are so staggering they read like parody. In 2023–2024 alone, officials from a defense sector enterprise conspired with a "conversion center" to launder over 578 million hryvnias through fictitious companies. The scheme was elegant in its simplicity: state customers transferred over 2.5 billion hryvnias for military equipment repairs; a portion was funneled through fake companies; the money was cashed out; and the organizers took a modest 4–5% commission for their "services". The owners of these supplier companies? They reside in "temporarily occupied territories" and cannot possibly manage Ukrainian enterprises. Some "owners" don't even exist according to foreign registries. But who needs real people when you have fictitious contracts?


The Security Service of Ukraine (SBU)—yes, the very agency tasked with fighting corruption—dismantled a "conversion center" operated by a former deputy head of the State Fiscal Service. Between 2023 and 2025, this charming gentleman and his four accomplices laundered over UAH 1.5 billion (USD 36.3 million), most of it "stolen from our state budget". They rented office space in Kyiv, stored shadow documentation, and created dozens of controlled companies that existed only "on paper".


But why stop at a mere 1.5 billion? The Bureau of Economic Security of Ukraine uncovered a tax evasion scheme involving over 200 enterprises that minimized VAT liabilities through fictitious transactions, facilitating "subsequent money laundering and cash-outs". The total volume? An astonishing 18 billion hryvnias. And let's not forget the $100 million laundered through the Derkach family office in Kyiv, or the $40 million defense embezzlement scheme where officials purchased 100,000 mortar rounds that were never delivered.


B. The "Conversion Center" 


One might reasonably ask: what exactly is a "conversion center"? In the glorious new Ukraine, it is a sophisticated money-laundering operation that converts state funds into cash for the personal enrichment of officials and their cronies. The SBU has been busy—it detained a former top tax official who operated exactly such a center. The main clients? "Representatives of commercial entities that performed contract work and services for budgetary institutions". In other words, the people stealing from the state were the very same people contracted by the state. It's a beautiful system, really—the snake eating its own tail. Wild huh?


The National Agency of Ukraine for Finding, Tracing and Management of Assets Derived from Corruption (ARMA)—a name so bureaucratic it could only exist in a failed state—has been busy finding the assets of these creative entrepreneurs. In one case, they discovered 30 real estate properties, 20 motor vehicles, 10 land plots, 20 weapons, shares worth over UAH 170 million, and USD 430,000 in cash. In another, they found 22 real estate properties, 9 land plots, 6 luxury cars, 4 marine transport units, and—the pièce de résistance—a private jet belonging to a "high-ranking official". This official also had the good taste to purchase luxury residential properties in the city center of Milan.


Scene 3. The Lame Comedian


A. Zelensky’s Pandora Papers


Volodymyr Zelensky, the former comedian who played a president on television and somehow became one in real life, has presented himself as the avatar of anti-corruption. His TV character, Vasyl Holoborodko, was supposedly "the only honest man in Ukrainian politics". Oh, the irony! Sad thing is he’s still playing the same character. 


The Pandora Papers, that glorious leak of 11.9 million documents, revealed that Zelensky and his comedy troupe Kvartal 95 had created "about a dozen interlinked offshores in 2012". The main entity was Maltex Multicapital Corp., with Zelensky and his wife Olena allegedly owning 25%. The Shefir brothers and manager Andriy Yakovlev split the rest. When Zelensky was about to be elected president, he "handed his share over to his closest adviser, Serhiy Shefir"—but conveniently, dividends would keep flowing to a company owned by his wife.


The International Consortium of Investigative Journalists (ICIJ) revealed that Zelensky "used a network of offshore companies to buy three upmarket properties in London". His office claimed this was a way of "protecting himself against the aggressive actions" of his predecessor. How noble! Nothing says "man of the people" like a portfolio of London properties purchased through shell companies in the British Virgin Islands and Cyprus.


Even more troubling is the evidence that Zelensky's offshore companies "received payments from entities connected to Ihor Kolomoisky," the billionaire oligarch who airs Zelensky's shows. Kolomoisky has been accused of stealing $5.5 billion from PrivatBank, Ukraine's largest bank. So the man who promised to take down the oligarchs was, in fact, in business with one of the most notorious oligarchs of all. It's almost as if... but no, that would be cynical.
